subject: URGENT: Aperture Financial — regional AZ failover request and SLA impact
messages:
From: Chris Yang <chris@aperturefin.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <ops@aperturefin.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike — 5xx + p95 latency rising > Aperture prod (US-EAST-1)

Jonas —

We started seeing a sharp increase in 5xx (from 0.2% baseline to ~8%) and p95 token latency climbing from ~85ms to ~760ms starting around 07:30 PDT. This is affecting our transaction enrichment flows and causing a backlog in our message queues. Our customers are seeing timeouts in the UI and a few payment retries.

Attached network traces and a short latency graph. Our SRE asks whether you can fail traffic away from us-east-1 to an alternate region (we prefer us-west-2) while you investigate — we need a mitigation window ASAP.

What we care about:
- Immediate reduction in 5xx and p95 latency (customer-facing impact)
- No data loss for in-flight requests (we rely on KV cache for session affinity)
- ETA for rollback vs permanent cross-region steer.

Please advise. If we need to sign any temporary routing consent, we can do that but want written confirmation of the steps and expected timeline.

— Chris Yang
VP Engineering, Aperture Financial
attachments: network-trace-logs-0506.txt, latency-timeseries-0506.png
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Chris Yang <chris@aperturefin.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike — 5xx + p95 latency rising > Aperture prod (US-EAST-1)

Chris — thanks for the signal and the traces. We're on it.

Quick summary of what we'll do in the next 90 minutes unless you object:
1) Activate controlled geo-steer to us-west-2 for 60% of Aperture's traffic (can be adjusted in 10% steps).
2) Throttle non-critical background batching for the account to free slots for interactive traffic.
3) Put a temporary model-variant pin (quantized v2-small) for new requests to reduce per-token CPU and memory pressure.
4) Keep KV cache TTLs intact; we will not flush caches unless forced — there will be cold-start penalty for a small portion of requests.

We need Aperture's consent to shift routing. If you reply with "GO" I will initiate and loop in Hannah (on-call routing) to execute and Connor for account ops. Vanessa, can you handle the customer comms and confirm whether an SLA credit conversation should be opened now or post-PM?

I will post updates to BR-7834 and share live metrics.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Connor Obrien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike — operational steps and caveats

On Thu, May 6, 2027 at 08:22 AM Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> Chris — thanks for the signal and the traces. We're on it.

Executing a controlled cross-region diversion is the right short-term mitigation. A few technical notes and risks so the customer and execs have context:
- Capacity check: us-west-2 has warm pools with ~1.6x headroom at current commit; we should be safe for a 60% diversion but monitor QPS.
- Cache behavior: session affinity will see cache misses for diverted requests; warmup will take ~15–30 minutes. Expect an initial p95 bump for a subset of users.
- KV and streaming: we will continue to write events back to Aperture's retention store; no synchronous writes will be dropped.
- Model pin: switching to v2-small-quant (4-bit) reduces latency variance but changes token-level quality slightly — we'll gate with a 5k-randomized prompt test.
- Rollback plan: if errors persist or p95 doesn't improve in 20 minutes, we will revert and open the next mitigation (rate-limiting or prioritized lanes).

Runbook steps (abbreviated):
1) Set routing policy aperturefin.com -> us-west-2 (weight 60%).
2) Disable batch job window for customer ID APTF-3245 for 90m.
3) Pin model variant on route to v2-small-quant.
4) Start live tracing and stream metrics to BR-7834.

I'll execute on GO from Chris.

— Hannah Schmitt
SRE Lead, Regional Routing — Redwood Inference

Thanks for the context. From a commercial/account perspective:
- Please confirm "GO" for the routing change. We'll keep the diversion temporary and provide live updates every 15 minutes.
- Aperture is an SLA customer; we should offer a short-term goodwill credit. I recommend offering a credit equal to one full day of average consumption now, with a postmortem credit adjustment after root-cause (we can escalate larger if the PM shows extended degradation).
- I am on standby to join any postmortem bridge and to draft the customer update.

If you confirm GO, we'll proceed and I will coordinate the comms with your SRE and leadership.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com, connor_obrien@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 14:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Aperture — mitigation complete; executive summary and next steps

For exec visibility — summary below and actions requested. Forwarding the customer thread for context.

Summary (ops):
- At 08:46 PDT we activated controlled geo-steer: 60% of Aperture traffic moved to us-west-2.
- By 09:10 PDT overall 5xx for Aperture dropped from ~7.8% to 1.2%. P95 latency improved from ~760ms to ~120ms for diverted traffic; overall customer-visible p95 is ~190ms (weighted).
- We pinned the route to v2-small-quant to reduce tail variance; quality checks (5k-sample) show minimal regressions for the enrichment prompts used by Aperture.
- No KV writes were lost; there was a transient cold-start window for ~18 minutes while caches warmed in us-west-2.

Commercial:
- Vanessa has offered an immediate goodwill credit of 1 day of average consumption; she requests approval to finalize and communicate.

Open items / next steps:
1) Approve the goodwill credit (Vanessa) — suggested cap: $18k (estimated).
2) Postmortem: SREs to produce RCA and difference report comparing kernel selection and disk I/O anomaly in us-east-1. (Hannah) — target delivery 2027-05-07 EOD.
3) Long-term mitigation: consider a higher baseline commit in us-east-1 or adding an additional warm pool. (Infrastructure)

Requesting confirmation from Marissa (Head of Customer Reliability) and Connor (CS lead) that the commercial approach is acceptable. Also marking this for VP-level awareness in the 15:00 PT leadership sync.

Metrics and logs are attached and available at BR-7834.

— Jonas Weber
Director, Customer Reliability — Redwood Inference
